STATEMENT OF TRAVELLING EXPENSES FROM 5th April 1940
AND USA AND SOUTH AMERICAN INCOME
FROM 25th June 1940 to 5th April 1941

Income from Viking Press.................... £ 1,591.34
(as per statement)
Income from Jacques Chambrun, ................ £ 1,252.50
New York, for articles in Magazines
Lectures in Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay... £ 3,600.00
                                     Total: £ 6,443.84

Travelling expenses for 2 persons.
Approximate fares:

Steamship tickets from England to Brazil
and board expenses.......................... £ 560.00

Airplane Rio - Sao Paulo and Return ..........      60.00

Airplane Rio - Buenos Aires and Return .........    430.00

Airplane Buenos Aires - Montevideo and Return....   50.00

Railway expenses in Argentina ................      80.00

Airplane Rio - Newyork .......................     780.00

Special expenses for luggage .................      90.00

Other travelling expenses including hotels,
car-fares, representation, telephone, stationery
and small disbursements ......................   4,320.00
                                     {9 Dollar pro person and day}
Cables and postage............................     180.00
                                     Total:   6,550.00

                                     Less income as stated: 6,443.84
                                     Deficit : £ 106.16

Address for air-mail: c/o Viking Press, 18 East 48th Street, Newyork
- later mail: c/o Editora Guanabara, 132 Rua Ouvidor, Rio de Janeiro
                                                              (Brazil)

                                     42 West 58th Street
                                     New York City

                                     2nd April, 1941

Binder, Hamlyn & Co.
River Plate House
12 South Place,
London E.C.2
ENGLAND

Dear Mr.Wilmot ,

I wrote you already from Rio to ask you as
my accountant about my position with regard to taxation
as I have been away from England since last June.

I have not yet received your reply and, there-
fore, do not know whether I am subject to income tax for the
{entire} last year or not. Anyway, I would like to facilitate your
task by giving you once more a statement on my position.

As you know, I left for South America last
June and have given in Brazil, Argentine and Uruguay a
series of lectures which I am asked to continue. During the
dead summer season in South America I have been here in USA
for further negotiations and the publication of a book on
Brazil which is, as you will understand, of special importance
in this moment. Under the prevailing circumstances I do not
see any possibility for me to earn a living in England or to
make myself useful while there. On the other hand, in the
Western Hemisphere I can achieve both aims, as I hope that I
will, for the time being, be able to make a modest living and
also to be of some use to our cause.

In order to enable you to prepare an income tax
return, I asked my sister-in-law, Mrs.Altmann, to give you all
{except the American} the details about my income from royalties/and investments
{which I did send you} during the taxable year. I myself have not been able to get any
{directly together with} regular statements, travelling from one country of South America
{my travelling expenses} to the other without possibility of receiving mail regularly
{on the lecture tour} owing to difficult communications which, among other reasons,
may also have caused the loss of some letters.
                                     {(European income)}
You will not be surprised that my literary {work}
has considerably decreased in this year of war, as in all the
occupied countries my books have immediately been suppressed
by the Nazis, and my literary activity was hampered by travelling
and lecturing.

As to my lecture tour, I told you before my
departure about an arrangement with the Ministry that I would
have to support myself abroad by lectures and literary work,
and that an eventual deficit should be covered only up to the
amount of two hundred pounds.
pages.notes: Typoskript mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen in violetter Tinte am linken Rand und im Text.

pages.transcription:
- II - 2nd April 1941

So far I have managed to support myself and, as
you will see from the enclosed statement, the deficit incurred
until now is rather small. I hope that I shall be able to
conclude new agreements which will enable me not to have to
apply for any money transfer from England. Since I am away,
I have been dependent with my wife on my activities here only,
as also the last of my foreign investments have been called up
by the Treasury, so that the equivalent in pounds must have been
already credited to my account with the Westminster Bank in
London.

You will see from the enclosed statement, which is
made up on US-Dollar basis, that I had an income of $ 6,443.84 ,
while my expenses amounting to $ 6,550.00 were somewhat higher,
so that the deficit of $ 106.16, i.e.£ 26.10.-, is up to now
much smaller than anticipated in my discussions with the Mini-
stry.

I suppose that you will find the amount of $ 4,320.00
for living expenses and other disbursements self-explanatory.
This amount would mean that I and my wife had spent for board,
fares, representation, telephone, stationery and other similar
disbursements less than $18.00 in the daily average during a
period of nine months. As you will probably imagine the condit-
ions under which I have to live here and especially in South
America, these travelling expenses cannot be considered high
and could really not be reduced.

I further wish to mention that I have not made any
deduction for the ample secretarial and translation work,
because all this work had been done by Mrs.Zweig, so that I did
not need any secretary or translator.

I hope that my sister-in-law, Mrs. Altmann, who has
dealt with all my correspondence since my departure, will have
no difficulties in giving you all necessary details.

Would you please be so kind as to confirm receipt
of this letter in duplicate sending one copy of your letter (airmail)
c/o Viking Press, 18 East 48th Street, New York City, and
another c/o Editora Guanabara, 132, Rua Ouvidor, Rio de Janeiro,
as my future plans are still uncertain, when I have to return there.

Thanking you in anticipation for your assistance and
expecting your reply to this letter and my letter from Rio,
I am

Yours very truly

Enc.

resnets. She has not much luck with me for I am often frightfully
depressed. This new war which is in any case a relief for Britain
means again destruction of numberless individual lives and happi
ness, it will result in a starvation of millions and especially
the Jews in the border country will be suffering as never before.
In Spain, in occupied France the lack of food is terrific and Europe
like but in the beginning - never has a single man brought so much
misery over the world than this beast Hitler. One is ashamed to see
here the abundance of food and everything, - that only what is
wasted every day and thrown away {in the restaurants} could feed a population. It
makes not so happy to be on this side if one has an instinct of
solidarity! And to think that all this will become worse and worse
for our mankind - you are much younger and will see after
the victory a better world but I with my "three lives" feel that
my generation has become superfluous. We have been a failure and
have no more right to give advise to the new one.
